description: The plot illustrates how vocabulary size changes as a function of the number of iterations for three languages (Spanish, Chinese, and Japanese), shown as three colored lines with faint same-colored bands around them and a separate gray diagonal reference line. The x-axis is labeled “Number of Iterations,” uses a linear scale, and runs from 0 to 500 with regularly spaced tick labels at 100-iteration intervals. The y-axis is labeled “Vocabulary Size,” uses a linear scale, and spans from 0 to 5000 with tick labels at 1000-unit intervals. The Spanish series is a blue solid line (no visible markers) that increases steadily from approximately 0 at iteration 0 to about 3300 at iteration 500, with a near-linear rise throughout. The Chinese series is an orange solid line (no visible markers) that also rises steadily from about 0 at iteration 0 to roughly 3100 at iteration 500. The Japanese series is a green solid line (no visible markers) increasing from about 0 at iteration 0 to around 3250–3300 at iteration 500. A gray solid diagonal line runs from (0, 0) to approximately (500, 5000), forming a straight reference trend across the panel.
